subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Security Misconfiguration
description: A micro-lesson that makes Security Misconfiguration usable.

hook.text: A server runs with debug mode on in production. Error pages show database credentials to every visitor.

buildup.text: Security misconfiguration means using default settings, open ports, or verbose errors in production.

discovery.text: Hardening checklists cover disabling defaults, removing sample apps, and restricting error verbosity.

twist.text: Cloud services launch with permissive defaults on purpose—for ease of setup. Production needs lockdown.

climax.text: An automated configuration scanner flags 15 issues. Fixing them before launch prevents exposure entirely.

punchline.text: Defaults are for development. Production demands hardening.

quiz.question: What is a common security misconfiguration?
